summary: Server-side CHOP for keeping timelines in multiple TouchDesigner processes within a frame of each other and optionally forwarding extra CHOP channels to Sync In clients.
key_concepts: Sync Out CHOP is the server side of a TouchDesigner Pro Sync In/Sync Out setup for keeping multiple processes within a single frame.
A sync group has one Sync Out process and one or more Sync In client processes.
Sync clients should have Realtime off, and all client and server monitors should use the same refresh rate.
The Sync CHOPs pause their own timelines until all Sync In/Out CHOPs have cooked, with Sync Out ahead of the Sync In clients.
Client processes can come online or go offline, and Sync Out can time out, temporarily ignore, or permanently ban unreliable clients.
Sync Out can forward extra input CHOP channels to Sync In clients, and Info DAT/Info CHOP diagnostics expose client replies, timeout totals, include state, and sync delay.

key_params.note: Multicast address used by the Sync group

key_params.name: port
key_params.note: Network port for the Sync group

key_params.name: localaddress
key_params.note: Local NIC address for multi-adapter machines

key_params.name: timeout
key_params.note: Maximum wait for synchronization signals in milliseconds

key_params.name: clienttimeouts
key_params.note: Consecutive client timeouts before the client is ignored until it replies on time again

key_params.name: banclients
key_params.note: Allow clients to be banned after timeouts

key_params.name: banclienttimeouts
key_params.note: Total timeouts before banning a client

common_gotchas: Official docs list Sync Out CHOP as TouchDesigner Pro only.
Sync Out waits for Sync In clients; failures or timeouts can slow every participating process.
Extra CHOP input channels sent through Sync Out are received by Sync In clients.
Use Info DAT on Sync Out to inspect clients, include flags, timeout totals, and client paths.
Client processes should disable Realtime, and all client/server monitors should use the same refresh rate.
Windows firewall can block discovery or communication.
